P1.evidence: Cleanest open in the batch. Frame delivered in full and agreed in one move: 'took a look at your application, got some of the details about what you're looking for, but really just want to understand and go a bit deeper on what's going on with your fitness right now, what you're looking to accomplish, what some of the challenges have been. And then from there, if we can help with that, I'll go into all the details about what we do, if that sounds good' — answered 'Yeah. Sounds good.' P1a partial: the application was acknowledged but nothing from it was actually read back, so the prospect got no sense of having been read.

P2.evidence: Five clean hits, the strongest baseline in the batch on everything except the one thing that mattered. Training reality established honestly — 'are you done with that program? Are you ready to start another program right away?' produced 'I'm doing nothing. I haven't lifted a finger in months.' Results from current effort nailed the key diagnostic: 99% of the 47 lb came from diet, 'I literally worked out for like two weeks.' Diet asked properly and followed through protein powders and hunger cues. Sleep and energy are the first genuine hits on those checks anywhere in this batch — 'Do you feel like your energy is mostly just from the lack of sleep? You said you're only getting maybe four or five hours?' Against that: P2c is a miss with weight behind it. The prospect opened the call by describing a hospital admission for presyncope with unexplained cause, and no health-conditions question was ever asked — not what was tested, not what was ruled out, not whether he is under anyone's care. Occupation was never asked; age and height were never established.

P3.evidence: The first half ran well. 'What's the end outcome that you're trying to achieve?' produced the six-pack and muscle goals; 'anything else on your end, fitness wise... maybe mobility or endurance or athleticism?' cleared the function questions; 'is there anything else that you're looking to maybe get back in shape for? Like you mentioned basketball?' produced the energy and sleep material. The bridge ran too: 'is there anything that's pushing you to stay in shape? Any bigger goals, perhaps, or any longer term motivation?' And then the deepest answer on the call was met with nothing. He said 'I've got a family, I'd love to see the next generation and grow up' and 'there's living and there's living', and the rep replied 'Being alive and living, I guess you could say. Yeah. Okay. Makes sense' and changed the subject. Four children aged 19, 12, 6 and 2, a father who nearly blacked out eight months ago, and 'who else does that impact' was never asked. When the kids did come up 25 minutes later it was as a time-constraint probe.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase anywhere in this batch. Past attempts covered fully — the current men-over-40 programme, seven and a half years vegan, assorted fad diets, a 5K. What happened with it: 'with this program, have they worked with you to try to maybe tailor it to your schedule?' produced 'No, not really. There's videos, you follow the videos, you kind of check the boxes when you're done with the app, but there's not a feedback loop. There's not a one-on-one component.' Why it did not stick was pushed on properly, including a clean clarifying interrupt — 'Sorry, what doesn't seem achievable?' The blocker was isolated and pressure-tested against his life: the travel schedule, the four kids, and the corroborating detail that two of his friends on the same programme also dropped the exercise half. P4f is partial only because the prospect got there himself before the rep asked: 'it's not really so much about the plan as it is about the mindset... the question is not you, the question is me.'

P5.evidence: Absent, on a call where the consequence had already physically happened. A hospital admission at his heaviest ever weight, an unexplained near-blackout, four children, and a stated fear of the men his age who 'are already starting to break down' — none of it was ever turned forward. No 'what does the next two years look like if nothing changes', no 'are you willing to settle for that', no line in the sand. When he later said the blocker was his own follow-through, the script's instruction is explicit — return to Phase 5 — and instead the rep went to an abstract mindset question.

P6.evidence: Both moves ran but in the wrong order and after the stall. P6a came at 00:49:45, after 'let me think on it': 'do you feel like maybe anything's missing that you would need to get results? Or do you feel like it would even work for you?' — answered with a full endorsement, 'the plan doesn't sound like it's flawed... it'll work for me if I do it.' P6b arrived as 'are you ready to actually lock into something?' and got 'Exactly. Yeah. That's the question' — an unresolved answer that was never pursued. P6c is a clear miss: the prospect asked for the price directly at 00:44:45 and got it with no commitment banked, and when hesitation surfaced the rep did not return to Phase 5.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. Price was presented, the prospect asked to think, and the call ended without an ask, a link, a deposit or a booked follow-up. Nothing in the phase was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Textbook trigger — 'Let me think on it. I'm not going to make a decision right this second.' Move one ran and worked: the belief check produced an unqualified yes on the programme. Then nothing. No 'what makes you feel it can', no 'so what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now'. The last of those was sitting in the open: this is a man who described exactly that pattern himself — 'I can't tell you how many times I knew that I absolutely had to lose weight, but my mindset wasn't there and I just never followed through, a few days messing around, kind of doing it, and then just gone, done.' He described the failure mode and was allowed to walk into it.

The doubt was self-directed rather than offer-directed — 'the question is not you, the question is me' — which is squarely OE territory. One move was attempted, a version of run-toward-pleasure versus away-from-pain: 'have you been focusing on the results of you getting in better shape, losing the weight, having more energy... or have you been focusing on the process, which is like, I got to do all this and that sucks?' It was delivered so unclearly that the prospect said 'I'm not sure I understood the question', and after a rephrase the answer went nowhere and the rep dropped it. None of BRIDGE, PLANE, BURNED BEFORE or 'how will you know if you never actually try' ran.

'A lot of money, a lot of money' and 'it's a commitment. That's a lot.' None of the play ran — no isolation, no HOW-not-SHOULD reframe, no financial picture, no plan structured. He asked directly whether it could be paid over time and got 'we can probably figure out something', with no financing partner or instalment figure named, on the same week the rep walked two other prospects through Payvo and PayPal links. The rep also introduced a damaging comparison unprompted: 'It's definitely more expensive than a trainer or something.'
His wife rang in the middle of the price presentation and he declined to take it, but he never made the decision contingent on her.
No timing objection — he wants to start and has already left the exercise half of his current programme behind.

A script gap worth logging: the prospect wants to buy only the training half and keep his existing nutrition programme, which the rep allowed — 'if you want to keep following the nutrition plan that you're already on, you're more than welcome to do that if you just want the exercise.' There is no move for a prospect paying full price for two of three pillars, and no reframe was attempted on what the Primal Eating Protocol would add over what already took 47 lb off him.

notes: Best P1 and best P4 in the batch — the root-cause work here was genuinely excellent and produced a precisely diagnosed blocker — and then the two phases that convert diagnosis into a decision, P5 and P6, did not run in the right order or at all. The prospect handed over a health emergency, four children and a named failure pattern, and none of the three became a reason to act today. Coaching action: when a prospect says the obstacle is his own follow-through, that is the signal to go back to Phase 5, not forward to a mindset conversation. Safety action first though: he disclosed an unexplained presyncope episode in his opening answer and no health question was asked at any point.
